{{Short description|Concept in mathematics}}
In mathematics, the '''free factor complex'''  (sometimes also called the '''complex of free factors''') is a [[free group]] counterpart of the notion of the [[curve complex]] of a finite type surface.
The free factor complex was originally introduced in a 1998 paper of [[Allen Hatcher]] and [[Karen Vogtmann]].<ref name=HV/> Like the curve complex, the free factor complex is known to be [[δ-hyperbolic space|Gromov-hyperbolic]]. The free factor complex plays a significant role in the study of large-scale geometry of [[Out(Fn)|<math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>]].

==Formal definition==

For a free group <math>G</math> a ''proper free factor'' of <math>G</math> is a [[subgroup]] <math>A\le G</math> such that <math>A\ne \{1\}, A\ne G</math> and that there exists a subgroup <math> B\le G</math> such that <math>G=A\ast B</math>.

Let <math> n\ge 3</math> be an integer and let <math>F_n</math> be the [[free group]] of rank <math>n</math>. The '''free factor complex''' <math> \mathcal F_n</math> for <math>F_n</math> is a [[simplicial complex]] where:

(1) The 0-cells are the [[conjugacy class]]es in <math>F_n</math> of proper free factors of <math>F_n</math>, that is 
:<math>\mathcal F_n^{(0)}=\{[A] | A\le F_n \text{ is a proper free factor of } F_n \}.</math>

(2) For <math>k\ge 1</math>, a <math>k</math>-simplex in <math> \mathcal F_n</math> is a collection of <math>k+1</math> distinct 0-cells <math>\{v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k\}\subset  \mathcal F_n^{(0)}</math> such that there exist free factors <math>A_0,A_1,\dots, A_k</math> of <math>F_n</math> such that <math>v_i=A_i</math> for <math>i=0,1,\dots, k</math>, and that <math>A_0\le A_1\le \dots \le A_k</math>.  [The assumption that these 0-cells are distinct implies that <math>A_i\ne A_{i+1}</math> for <math> i=0,1,\dots, k-1</math>]. In particular, a 1-cell is a collection <math> \{[A], [B]\}</math> of two distinct 0-cells where <math>A,B\le F_n</math> are proper free factors of <math>F_n</math> such that <math>A\lneq B</math>.

For <math>n=2</math> the above definition produces a complex with no <math>k</math>-cells of dimension <math>k\ge 1</math>. Therefore, <math>\mathcal F_2</math> is defined slightly differently. One still defines <math>\mathcal F_2^{(0)}</math> to be the set of conjugacy classes of proper free factors of <math>F_2</math>; (such free factors are necessarily infinite cyclic). Two distinct 0-simplices <math>\{v_0,v_1\}\subset  \mathcal F_2^{(0)}</math> determine a 1-simplex in <math>\mathcal F_2</math> if and only if there exists a free basis <math>a,b</math> of <math>F_2</math> such that <math>v_0=[\langle a\rangle], v_1=[\langle b\rangle]</math>.
The complex <math>\mathcal F_2</math> has no <math>k</math>-cells of dimension <math>k\ge 2</math>.

For <math>n\ge 2</math> the 1-skeleton <math>\mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math> is called the '''free factor graph''' for <math>F_n</math>.

==Main properties==

* For every integer <math>n\ge 3</math> the complex <math>\mathcal F_n</math> is connected, locally infinite, and has dimension <math>n-2</math>. The complex <math>\mathcal F_2</math> is connected, locally infinite, and has dimension 1.
* For <math>n=2</math>, the graph <math>\mathcal F_2</math> is isomorphic to the [[Farey graph]]. 
* There is a natural [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] of [[Out(Fn)|<math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>]] on <math>\mathcal F_n</math> by simplicial automorphisms. For a ''k''-simplex <math>\Delta=\{[A_0],\dots, [A_k]\}</math> and <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> one has <math>\varphi \Delta:=\{[\varphi(A_0)],\dots, [\varphi(A_k)]\}</math>.
*For <math>n\ge 3</math> the complex <math>\mathcal F_n</math> has the [[homotopy type]] of a wedge of spheres of dimension <math>n-2</math>.<ref name=HV>{{cite journal
| last1=Hatcher | first1=Allen | authorlink1=Allen Hatcher
| last2=Vogtmann | first2=Karen | authorlink2=Karen Vogtmann
| title=The complex of free factors of a free group
| journal=[[Quarterly Journal of Mathematics]] | series=Series 2
| volume=49
| date=1998
| issue=196
| pages=459–468
| doi=10.1093/qmathj/49.4.459| arxiv=2203.15602
}}</ref>
*For every integer <math>n\ge 2</math>, the free factor graph <math>\mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math>, equipped with the simplicial metric (where every edge has length 1), is a connected graph of infinite diameter.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Kapovich | first1=Ilya | authorlink1=Ilya Kapovich
| last2=Lustig | first2=Martin
| title=Geometric intersection number and analogues of the curve complex for free groups
| journal=[[Geometry & Topology]]
| volume=13
| date=2009
| issue=3
| pages=1805–1833
| doi=10.2140/gt.2009.13.1805 | doi-access=free| arxiv=0711.3806
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Behrstock | first1=Jason
| last2=Bestvina | first2=Mladen | authorlink2=Mladen Bestvina
| last3=Clay | first3=Matt
| title=Growth of intersection numbers for free group automorphisms
| journal=[[Journal of Topology]]
| volume=3
| date=2010
| issue=2
| pages=280–310
| doi=10.1112/jtopol/jtq008| arxiv=0806.4975
}}</ref>
*For every integer <math>n\ge 2</math>, the free factor graph <math>\mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math>, equipped with the simplicial metric, is [[δ-hyperbolic space|Gromov-hyperbolic]]. This result was originally established by [[Mladen Bestvina]] and Mark Feighn;<ref  name=BF14>{{cite journal
| last1=Bestvina | first1=Mladen | authorlink1=Mladen Bestvina
| last2=Feighn | first2=Mark
| title=Hyperbolicity of the complex of free factors
| journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]
| volume=256
| date=2014
| pages=104–155
| doi=10.1016/j.aim.2014.02.001 | doi-access=free| arxiv=1107.3308
}}</ref> see also <ref name=KR>{{cite journal
| last1=Kapovich | first1=Ilya | authorlink1=Ilya Kapovich
| last2=Rafi | first2=Kasra
| title=On hyperbolicity of free splitting and free factor complexes
| journal=[[Groups, Geometry, and Dynamics]]
| volume=8
| date=2014
| issue=2
| pages=391–414
| doi=10.4171/GGD/231 | doi-access=free| arxiv=1206.3626
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Hilion | first1=Arnaud
| last2=Horbez | first2=Camille
| title=The hyperbolicity of the sphere complex via surgery paths
| journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]
| volume=730
| date=2017
| pages=135–161
| doi=10.1515/crelle-2014-0128| arxiv=1210.6183
}}</ref> for subsequent alternative proofs.
*An element <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> acts as a loxodromic isometry of <math>\mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math> if and only if <math>\varphi</math> is [[fully irreducible automorphism|fully irreducible]].<ref name=BF14/>
*There exists a coarsely Lipschitz coarsely <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>-equivariant coarsely surjective map <math>\mathcal{FS}_n\to \mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math>, where <math>\mathcal{FS}_n</math> is the [[free splittings complex]].  However, this map is not a [[quasi-isometry]]. The free splitting complex is also known to be [[δ-hyperbolic space|Gromov-hyperbolic]], as was proved by Handel and Mosher.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Handel | first1=Michael | authorlink1=Michael Handel
| last2=Mosher | first2=Lee
| title=The free splitting complex of a free group, I: hyperbolicity
| journal=[[Geometry & Topology]]
| volume=17
| date=2013
| issue=3
| pages=1581–1672
| mr=3073931
| doi=10.2140/gt.2013.17.1581 | doi-access=free| arxiv=1111.1994
}}</ref> 
*Similarly, there exists a natural coarsely Lipschitz coarsely <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>-equivariant coarsely surjective map <math>CV_n\to \mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math>, where <math>CV_n</math> is the (volume-ones normalized) [[Outer space (mathematics)|Culler–Vogtmann Outer space]], equipped with the symmetric Lipschitz metric. The map <math>\pi</math> takes a geodesic path in <math>CV_n</math> to a path in <math>\mathcal FF_n</math> contained in a uniform Hausdorff neighborhood of the geodesic with the same endpoints.<ref name=BF14/>
*The hyperbolic boundary <math>\partial \mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math> of the free factor graph can be identified with the set of equivalence classes of "arational" <math>F_n</math>-trees in the boundary <math>\partial CV_n</math> of the Outer space <math>CV_n</math>.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Bestvina | first1=Mladen | authorlink1=Mladen Bestvina
| last2=Reynolds | first2=Patrick
| title=The boundary of the complex of free factors
| journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]
| volume=164
| date=2015
| issue=11
| pages=2213–2251
| doi=10.1215/00127094-3129702| arxiv=1211.3608
}}</ref>
*The free factor complex is a key tool in studying the behavior of [[random walk]]s on <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> and in identifying the [[Poisson boundary]] of <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Horbez | first1=Camille
| title=The Poisson boundary of <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_N)</math>
| journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]
| volume=165
| date=2016
| issue=2
| pages=341–369
| doi=10.1215/00127094-3166308| arxiv=1405.7938
}}</ref>

==Other models==

There are several other models which produce graphs coarsely [[Out(Fn)|<math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>]]-equivariantly [[quasi-isometry|quasi-isometric]] to <math>\mathcal F_n^{(1)}</math>. These models include:

*The graph whose vertex set is <math>\mathcal F_n^{0}</math> and where two distinct vertices <math>v_0,v_1</math> are adjacent if and only if there exists a free product decomposition <math>F_n=A\ast B\ast C</math> such that <math>v_0=[A]</math> and <math>v_1=[B]</math>.
*The '''free bases graph''' whose vertex set is the set of <math>F_n</math>-conjugacy classes of free bases of <math>F_n</math>, and where two vertices <math>v_0,v_1</math> are adjacent if and only if there exist free bases <math>\mathcal A, \mathcal B</math> of <math>F_n</math> such that <math>v_0=[\mathcal A], v_1=[\mathcal B]</math> and <math>\mathcal A\cap \mathcal B\ne \varnothing </math>.<ref name=KR/>
